newsitem.title: NORWAY: Saga makes moderate oil, gas discovery in North Sea.
newsitem.headline: Saga makes moderate oil, gas discovery in North Sea.

text.p: Saga Petroleum ASA has made a moderate oil and gas discovery in block 34/7 in the North Sea, the Oil Directorate said on Tuesday.
Exploration well 34/7-25 S was spudded southeast of the Tordis oilfield to a depth of 2,573 metres below sea level.
The well tested at 1,050 cubic metres per day of oil and 106,000 cubic metres per day of gas through a choke of 15.9 mm diameter.
The directorate said the test confirmed that the characteristics of the reservoir were good.

"The size of the discovery is still not known but is expected to be moderate," a directorate statement said. "Its location near to existing infrastructure may make it interesting for future development."
Further exploration in the area was under consideration, it said.

Operator Saga holds 7.7 percent of licence 089 and is partnered by Den norske stats oljeselskap AS with 55.4 percent, Esso with 10.5, Idemitsu with 9.6, Norsk Hydro ASA with 8.4, Elf Petroleum with 5.6 and Deminex with 2.8 percent.
